title: Making the acylium ion
subtitle: AlCl₃ pulls chloride from acetyl chloride

reactants.caption: acetyl chloride + aluminium chloride
reactants.learnerPrompt: Aluminium chloride is a Lewis acid. Show it binding to acetyl chloride.
hintTiers: Which atom of AlCl₃ is electron-poor, and which lone pair of acetyl chloride leads to a leaving group?
The chlorine of acetyl chloride uses a lone pair to bond to aluminium. One arrow.
Cl4 lone pair → new Cl4–Al5 bond.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The carbonyl oxygen does bind AlCl₃, but that gives no leaving group. Bind the chlorine, so it can leave.

complex.caption: acetyl chloride–AlCl₃ complex
complex.learnerPrompt: The chlorine leaves as AlCl₄⁻. Draw how the acylium ion forms.
hintTiers: Losing chloride would leave the carbon short of electrons. Which neighbouring lone pair can make up for it?
The C–Cl bond breaks onto chlorine while an oxygen lone pair forms a second π bond to carbon. Two arrows.
O3 lone pair → π C2–O3; σ C2–Cl4 → lone pair on Cl4.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Chloride leaves, but the carbon is left with six electrons. Let the oxygen share another pair.

steps.explanationAfterStep: Coordinated to aluminium, the chlorine carries a positive charge: a much better leaving group.
CH₃–C≡O⁺ is linear. Its carbon is the electrophile; its octets make it stable enough not to rearrange.

mechanismSummary: Chlorine's lone pair coordinates to AlCl₃, making it a far better leaving group. It leaves as AlCl₄⁻ while the oxygen lone pair forms a C≡O⁺ triple bond: the acylium ion, the electrophile of Friedel–Crafts acylation. Every atom of the acylium ion has an octet, so unlike an alkyl cation it does not rearrange.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 21
